chemical_compatibility.description: Source SRC-CHEM-001 is a general aid and does not constitute a guarantee. Record chemical concentration and temperature exactly; missing or variable data shall fail closed to engineering review.

asme_viii_1_2023_check.title: ASME BPVC SECTION VIII DIVISION 1 - 2023 PLATE LISTING CHECK
asme_viii_1_2023_check.description: This sheet checks whether each preliminary pressure-vessel plate specification is listed in the applicable 2023 Division 1 material table. It does not verify allowable stress, exact material condition, design temperature, MDMT, impact testing or PWHT.

formula_cells.formula: =COUNTIF(G10:G73,"Corrected to ASME VIII-1 2023 listing")+COUNTIF(G10:G73,"Code-listed candidate; engineering selection required")

asme_ii_d_2021_check.title: ASME BPVC SECTION II, PART D (METRIC) 2021 - FAIL-CLOSED STRESS LOOKUP CHECK
asme_ii_d_2021_check.description: The sheet indexes exact Table 1A/1B plate records against the material guide. It does not select an allowable stress because design temperature is blank and several rows contain multiple candidate grades, classes, conditions or thickness records. No interpolation has been used. ASME BPVC II.D.M-2021 is an edition mismatch with the workbook's ASME BPVC VIII-1 2023 basis.

asme_ii_d_stress_records.title: ASME BPVC II.D.M-2021 - TABLE 1A / TABLE 1B PLATE STRESS RECORD INDEX
asme_ii_d_stress_records.description: Each row is a source record transcribed from the 2021 metric stress tables. Blank stress cells mean no published value at that temperature for the record. The source PDF controls. Italic/bold typography indicating time-dependent regimes is not represented in this index. Do not interpolate or select the highest value automatically. Full note text is now available in 'ASME II-D Note Library', with record-level applicability in 'ASME II-D Record Notes'.

asme_ii_d_note_library.title: ASME BPVC II.D.M-2021 - COMPLETE TABLE 1A / TABLE 1B NOTE LIBRARY
asme_ii_d_note_library.description: All 171 notes from the supplied Notes to Table 1A (pp. 160-162) and Notes to Table 1B (pp. 292-294) are transcribed below. Relationship columns connect each note to the 99 source records in 'ASME II-D Stress Records'. The governing ASME edition and source pages remain the design and audit authority; note applicability, material selection and interpolation must remain fail-closed.

asme_ii_d_record_notes.title: ASME BPVC II.D.M-2021 - NOTE APPLICABILITY BY STRESS RECORD
asme_ii_d_record_notes.description: Each stress record is linked to all table-level General Notes and to every coded note explicitly listed in its 'Note IDs' field. This sheet provides material-by-material note traceability without replacing engineering selection, code-edition alignment, or review of the governing ASME source.

basis_and_limitations.why_it_matters: Unlike pipe, plate generally has no separate B36-type dimensional standard. General requirements and material grade must both be shown.

basis_and_limitations.minimum_decision_check: Verify the exact ASME Section II material record accepted by the governing ASME VIII edition.

basis_and_limitations.why_it_matters: Impact-test exemptions and toughness depend on material, thickness, heat treatment and minimum design metal temperature.
basis_and_limitations.minimum_decision_check: Document MDMT, governing thickness and impact-test basis.

basis_and_limitations.why_it_matters: Corrosion, wet H2S, hydrogen attack, chloride SCC, sulfidation, naphthenic acid and caustic service may govern over strength.
basis_and_limitations.minimum_decision_check: Complete material selection report and damage-mechanism review.

basis_and_limitations.why_it_matters: Many SA-387 and other plate specifications include classes and mandatory heat-treatment conditions.
basis_and_limitations.minimum_decision_check: Select class, normalized/tempered or Q&T condition and PWHT basis.

basis_and_limitations.minimum_decision_check: Use the 2021 records only as an interim reference. Final design requires the exact plate record, class/condition, thickness, design temperature and a project-approved matched-edition code basis.

asme_ii_d_record_notes.full_note_text: Due to the relatively low yield strength of these materials, these higher stress values were established at temperatures where the short-time tensile properties govern to permit the use of these alloys where slightly greater deformation is acceptable. The stress values in this range exceed 66⅔% but do not exceed 90% of the yield strength at temperature. Use of these stresses may result in dimensional changes due to permanent strain. These stress values are not recommended for the flanges of gasketed joints or other applications where slight amounts of distortion can cause leakage or malfunction. For Section III applications, Table Y-2 lists multiplying factors that, when applied to the yield strength values shown in Table Y-1, will give allowable stress values that will result in lower levels of permanent strain.

The stress values in this range exceed 66⅔% but do not exceed 90% of the yield strength at temperature. Use of these stresses may result in dimensional changes due to permanent strain. These stress values are not recommended for the flanges of gasketed joints or other applications where slight amounts of distortion can cause leakage or malfunction. asme_ii_d_record_notes.full_note_text: Due to the relatively low yield strength of these materials, these higher stress values were established at temperatures where the short-time tensile properties govern to permit the use of these alloys where slightly greater deformation is acceptable. The stress values in this range exceed 66⅔% but do not exceed 90% of the yield strength at temperature. Use of these stresses may result in dimensional changes due to permanent strain. These stress values are not recommended for the flanges of gasketed joints or other applications where slight amounts of distortion can cause leakage or malfunction. For Section III applications, Table Y-2 lists multiplying factors that, when applied to the yield strength values shown in Table Y-1, will give allowable stress values that will result in lower levels of permanent strain.

asme_ii_d_record_notes.full_note_text: Due to the relatively low yield strength of these materials, these higher stress values were established at temperatures where the short-time tensile properties govern to permit the use of these alloys where slightly greater deformation is acceptable. The stress values in this range exceed 66⅔% but do not exceed 90% of the yield strength at temperature. Use of these stresses may result in dimensional changes due to permanent strain. These stress values are not recommended for the flanges of gasketed joints or other applications where slight amounts of distortion can cause leakage or malfunction. For Section III applications, Table Y-2 lists multiplying factors that, when applied to the yield strength values shown in Table Y-1, will give allowable stress values that will result in lower levels of permanent strain.

asme_ii_d_record_notes.full_note_text: Due to the relatively low yield strength of these materials, these higher stress values were established at temperatures where the short-time tensile properties govern to permit the use of these alloys where slightly greater deformation is acceptable. The stress values in this range exceed 66⅔% but do not exceed 90% of the yield strength at temperature. Use of these stresses may result in dimensional changes due to permanent strain. These stress values are not recommended for the flanges of gasketed joints or other applications where slight amounts of distortion can cause leakage or malfunction. For Section III applications, Table Y-2 lists multiplying factors that, when applied to the yield strength values shown in Table Y-1, will give allowable stress values that will result in lower levels of permanent strain.
